findings.title: All tested product orders should remain rejected
findings.detail: Eight nonbaseline outcomes gain1–9 lots but lose78–225 existing stable keys. No supplied migration/visual/gameplay/performance evidence justifies this city-wide replacement for a bounded rank1 intervention. Small incremental gains are not intrinsically invalid; rejection is based on their scope and churn relative to demonstrated benefit.

findings.title: Retained key does not mean retained parcel or equivalent city
findings.detail: Many retained stable keys have altered frames/membership, and0–4 retain their lot ID across fresh worlds. All alternate building/simulation/economy serializations differ. Buildings seed deterministic plans from assigned building IDs and class; authored pre-roll and loans then respond to actual capacity/state. No visual quality direction is measured.

findings.title: Comparator labels and exhaustiveness need qualification
findings.detail: ID order consistently gains8 in both seeds. shortest-first still combines weighted length with jitter, not strict length-only order. reverse-current reverses within-class priority while preserving class rank. Four comparators on two seeds do not exhaust coarse reordering or localized interventions.

findings.title: Fresh-world identity churn is not an executed historical-load failure
findings.detail: Each outcome is a fresh disposable startup. Existing-city regeneration can match retained stable keys; importing old saves under altered startup remains untested. Risks are real enough to withhold product acceptance, but no save corruption or migration failure was demonstrated.

limits: All ten full JSON run records, all lot lists, complete stored building/simulation serialization trees, gained/lost records and economy comparisons were read and traversed offline. No screenshots were requested or inspected because no alternative is advanced.
No live browser run, fresh build, product source edit, whole-game test, performance/memory or historical save/import test was performed by this critic.
Each variant/seed has one retained fresh-start run. Deterministic source does not substitute for repeated-run/restage verification; successful zero-error startup is the narrow pass flag.

Stored buildings are complete outputs of buildings.serialize(), not full runtime plans or rendered images. Serialized differences and source explain changed deterministic inputs; they do not demonstrate visible degradation or improvement.

The current comparison is self-comparison, so its equality booleans alone are tautological. Exact routed source bytes and independent current counts/source provenance provide the baseline scope check.

Stable key uses edge/side/original-front-cell and is unique in every stored run. Retained keys do not guarantee unchanged geometry, class, cells, numeric ID or building ID. Retained same-frame/membership counts are reported separately.

No actual generation edge sequence or raw slot runs are retained in R8x. All ten final counts are recomputed from complete lot lists; exact comparator code/hash is verified, but this audit does not independently rerun geometry/frontage generation.
Only road-class priority-preserving variants were tested. No claim that all order changes fail or that coordinated road redesign is mathematically necessary follows.

Higher jobs/cash/happiness in some variants are altered startup outcomes, not proven better gameplay, sustained finances or additional net usable city fabric. Larger claimed-key gain is not equal to additional lots.
No full rendered matrix/API/restage/retained-memory acceptance checks are necessary to keep unaccepted routed experiments rejected. Their absence is not a passed product gate.

nextOwnerSafePriority.task: Retain accepted order. Any future rank1 proposal should first demonstrate local legal frontage/run yield without global key replacement, or justify a larger explicit redesign with preservation/migration, visual, economy and performance evidence. The four rejected comparators provide negative evidence, not an impossibility theorem.
